title: TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours Rollover of Unused Hours and Expiry Extensions
content:
## Rollover

1. Where the expiring TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block's size allows rollover, its unused hours may roll into a new block that the client orders as a rollover order.
2. A new block qualifies to receive a rollover only when it is ordered within the size's rollover window, in calendar days before the expiring block's expiry date. The window opens that number of calendar days before the expiry date and closes at the end of the expiry date itself; an order on the opening day or on the expiry date is within it. The evidence is the expiring block's expiry date on its record.
3. The new block must be the same size or larger than the expiring block.
4. The rollover is posted on the day the new block is activated: the expiring block's balance, capped at its block hours times its rollover cap percentage divided by 100, rolls out of it and into the new block, any balance above the cap is forfeited, and the expiring block expires that day.
5. Rolled-in hours share the new block's expiry date and never roll over a second time.

Hypothetical cases: with a 60-day window and an expiry date of 30 June, the window opens on 1 May; an order on 30 April does not qualify and one on 1 May or 30 June does. A 40-hour block with a 25 percent cap and 14.00 hours left rolls 10.00 hours and forfeits 4.00; with 6.00 hours left it rolls all 6.00.

## Extension

6. Where the size allows extension, a block may instead be extended by the size's extension months, at most the size's maximum number of extensions.
7. An extension must be signed no later than the block's expiry date. The expiry date itself is the last day an extension can be signed: 0 days of lead are required, so a signature on the expiry date is in time and one on the following day is not.
8. > **This clause is no longer in force:** "The extension fee is the size's extension fee percentage of the hours balance valued at the rate per block hour, rounded half up to the cent, invoiced when the extension takes effect; a block whose hours were rolled out cannot be extended." The fee of an extension, every extension being bought on the authorized contact's signed order form, is now figured under the current extension fee basis and invoiced when the extension takes effect on that signature. A block whose hours were rolled out still cannot be extended.

superseded_clauses: The extension fee is extension_fee_pct percent of hours_balance valued at hourly_rate_usd, rounded half up to the cent, invoiced when the extension takes effect; a block whose hours were rolled out cannot be extended.
